args.body:
## Job
Make sure every new or edited team document in the docs project starts with the `Owner: docs-team` line, so the owner-line pre-merge check passes and the document matches the project convention.

## When to use
Whenever a ticket asks you to create or fill a file under `deliverables/`, `reports/`, `handbook/` or `minutes/` in the docs project (README.md: "Team documents live in deliverables/, reports/, handbook/ and minutes/"). Applies even when the ticket description or acceptance criteria only specify the body content and never mention an owner line, and even when `agenium.toml` shows an empty `[checks] pre_merge` value.

## Steps
1. Read `README.md` to confirm which folders the project treats as team-document folders; treat any file created there as a team document.
2. Read an existing team document (e.g. `deliverables/hello.txt` or `reports/weekly.txt`) to copy the exact convention: line 1 `Owner: docs-team`, then the requested body content on the following line(s).
3. Write the new file with `Owner: docs-team` as the very first line, then the body the ticket asks for. Do not put a BOM or a blank line before it.
4. Verify with a read-back: print the file line by line and check the first three bytes are `79,119,110` (`O`, `w`, `n`, i.e. no BOM) and that line 1 is exactly `Owner: docs-team`.
5. Only then report the acceptance criteria, citing the read-back output as evidence.

## Tools
- `read_file` / `list_dir` to inspect README.md and existing team documents.
- `write_file` (or the file tool, not `>` or `Set-Content -Encoding utf8`, which add a BOM/UTF-16) to create the file.
- `shell` with PowerShell for the verification read-back: `Get-Content <file>` plus `[IO.File]::ReadAllBytes(<file>)`.
- `grep` to confirm the required word is present.

## Proof
Evidence must be a command output, not a claim: show the numbered/printed lines of the new file (first line `Owner: docs-team`, body line containing the required word) and the byte check proving there is no BOM before `O`. A report that only says "the file was created with the owner line" without this read-back does not count.

args.body:
## Job
Create or fill a team document in a docs project so that it satisfies the project's owner-line rule (first line exactly `Owner: <team>`) and contains the requested content, verified at byte level.

## When to use
- A ticket asks to add or fill a file under a team-document directory such as `deliverables/`, `reports/`, `handbook/` or `minutes/`.
- The ticket description specifies only the body content and does not mention an owner line.
- Use it whenever the project may run a pre-merge check on document format, even if `[checks] pre_merge` in `agenium.toml` looks empty.

## Steps
1. List the worktree and read the project `README.md` to learn which directories hold team documents.
2. Read at least two existing documents in those directories. Copy the first line verbatim (in this project: `Owner: docs-team`) instead of guessing the team name.
3. Write the file with the owner line as the very first line, followed by the requested content on its own line. Write LF line endings and no UTF-8 BOM (use the file tool, not PowerShell `>` or `Set-Content`, which add a BOM or UTF-16).
4. Verify with a byte and regex check, not just by eyeballing: read the bytes, confirm the first bytes are `4F 77 6E 65 72 3A 20` (`Owner: `) and not `EF BB BF` (BOM), and confirm the content word matches as a whole word, e.g. `[IO.File]::ReadAllText((Resolve-Path path)) -match '(?m)^Owner: docs-team$'` and `-match '\bstandup\b'`.
5. Run `git status --porcelain` to confirm the new path is the only change, then report the file path, the byte-level evidence and the regex results.

## Tools
- Directory listing and glob tools to find existing team documents.
- File read/write/edit tools to create the document with UTF-8 (no BOM) content.
- Shell (PowerShell on Windows) for `[IO.File]::ReadAllBytes` / `ReadAllText`, regex checks and `git status`.

## Proof
The report must show evidence that anyone can re-run:
- the full path of the created file,
- the byte dump or at least the byte length plus the decoded first line proving `Owner: <team>` is line 1 with no BOM,
- the output of the whole-word regex check for the required content word (e.g. `contains word standup OK`),
- `git status --porcelain` output showing the change.
A claim of "file created" without the byte/regex output does not satisfy this skill.
